This method computes a tight 2D axis-aligned bounding box (AABB) for Quadratic Gaussian Splatting (QGS) primitives by approximating the primitive's boundary with tangent planes, avoiding the loose approximation of projecting 3D bounding box vertices [S1].

The claim states that the method computes a tight 2D AABB for QGS primitives by approximating the boundary with tangent planes to avoid the loose approximation of projecting 3D bounding box vertices. Source [S1] explicitly mentions that a straightforward approach (projecting vertices) results in a 'loose case' that 'significantly enlarges the 2D bounding box'. It then states, 'To address this, we construct a tighter bounding box using the quadric's tangent planes.' The notes further detail the process of using tangent planes at specific points to compute intersections, which aligns with the claim's description of the method.
